text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- The Christian Democrat national council reelected incumbent Gyorgy Giczy as party president Saturday with 133 votes to 102 for rival candidate Zsolt Semjen.

- The Free Democrats want to see a bdget than can offer security to citizens, is fair to the needy, and creates conditions for the advancement of future generations, House leader Istvan Szent-Ivanyi told reporters after the parliamentary group wrapped up two days of talks.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn is to meet with representatives of employers and employees in the Interest Coordination Council on Tuesday to discuss this year's earnings and expected wage increase for 1998.

- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy on Friday expressed hope that the government would pass the 1998 budget guidelines as early as next week, despite the 100 billion forint gap between the subsidy requests of the various ministries and theamount approved by the Finance Ministry (Sat).

- Malaysian Prime Minister Dato Seri Mahathir bin Mohammed begins a two-day visit to Hungary on Monday to promote bilateral relations in new areas, and further cooperation in technology, information sciences and education (also in Magyar Hirlap).
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs will address a NATO conference in Prague on Monday (also in Magyar Nemzet).

- The state privatisaton and holding co APV Rt will discuss the sale of Ringa Rt, the last state-owned meat company on Wednesday. However, the June 18 meeting of the Meat Industrialists Association announced that Pick has been awarded the tender.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said that the cabinet was considering holding a referendum on NATO membership this year (Sat).
